close_reason: Fixed in bf895d2: switched jscontact_module_alias_is_jmap_jscontact_types test from runtime assert_eq! to compile-time type-identity assertion via const fn pointers (const _ASSERT_ALIASED_SAME_AS_DIRECT, const _ASSERT_TOP_LEVEL_SAME_AS_DIRECT). The const items fail to typecheck if paths diverge — zero runtime cost. The deserialize calls survive as a runtime smoke-test.
description:
lib.rs:1144 `jscontact_module_alias_is_jmap_jscontact_types` is
written as:

```rust
let direct: jmap_jscontact_types::Name = serde_json::from_value(v.clone()).unwrap();
let aliased: crate::jscontact::Name = serde_json::from_value(v).unwrap();
// Both paths resolve to the same type; equality is well-defined.
assert_eq!(direct, aliased);
let top_level: Name = direct.clone();
assert_eq!(direct, top_level);
```

The comment says 'Both paths resolve to the same type'. The runtime
assert_eq! tests value equality, not type identity. The type-identity
check is already done at compile time by the type ascription
(`let aliased: crate::jscontact::Name = ...` would fail to compile
if the alias and the direct path resolved to different types — the
deserialize would still succeed for any `T: Deserialize`, but the
ascription would only typecheck if the path resolves correctly).

Idiomatic Rust for proving type identity at compile time:

```rust
// Compile-time-only — zero runtime cost, fails the build if the
// paths diverge.
const _ASSERT_SAME: fn(jmap_jscontact_types::Name) -> crate::jscontact::Name =
    |x| x;
const _ASSERT_TOP_LEVEL: fn(jmap_jscontact_types::Name) -> Name = |x| x;
```

…or, more conventionally, use `static_assertions::assert_type_eq_all!`.

What goes wrong: the current test passes for two distinct reasons:
(a) the paths resolve to the same type (the thing the test name
implies it's checking), and (b) the value happens to equal itself
after a round-trip through Deserialize. If a future refactor made
the alias re-export a thin newtype wrapper around the original Name
(implementing PartialEq with the original), the type-identity check
would silently regress to 'they're equal-valued' instead of 'they
are the same type'.

Mitigating factors (why this is opinion, not engineering):
1. The test name and comment together do communicate intent to a
   reader, even if the assert is not the right tool.
2. The cost of being wrong (test passes when alias diverges) is
   bounded — downstream callers using `crate::jscontact::Name` would
   notice a type mismatch at their use site.
3. The runtime assert is also incidentally exercising serde, which
   has independent value.

If kept as is, label is opinion. If acted on, the const-fn or
static_assertions form is the idiomatic Rust replacement and would
also let the test be removed from the `#[test]` set entirely (it
becomes a compile-time check).
title: jscontact_module_alias test uses runtime assert_eq! where compile-time type assertion is idiomatic Rust
